dedupe_keys.name: eu projects of common interest and projects of mutual interest pci and pmi list and interactive transparency map

description: Projects of Common Interest (PCIs) are the cross-border energy infrastructure projects that the European Union lists under its Trans-European Networks for Energy (TEN-E) regulation, and Projects of Mutual Interest (PMIs) are their counterparts with countries outside the EU, introduced by the 2022 revision. The European Commission page read on 2026-09-28 explains the selection criteria, the benefits (permits within 3.5 years, cross-border cost allocation, eligibility for Connecting Europe Facility funding), notes that the second Union list of PCIs and PMIs was adopted on 29 April 2026, and points to the PCI-PMI interactive map, a transparency platform giving each project's location, implementation plan, benefits and possible EU support; examples include the 700 MW Celtic Interconnector and the Baltic synchronisation completed on 9 February 2025. Coverage is the EU and neighbours, for electricity, gas, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and smart grid projects. Access is free; no licence is stated on the page. Caveats: the list names planned projects whose dates and capacities change, and bulk data export from the map was not checked. It supports capacity planning and future network scenarios for European power and gas models. No related EU project-list record is catalogued; ENTSO-E and ENTSOG plans complement it.
